I am talking, of course, about the restrictions on upvotes (until you reach 20 CCP, currently), downvotes (until you reach 100 CCP, currently), and the restrictions on commenting if you have too low CCP (-50, currently).

Restrictions on less-than-popular users encourage a community going toxic, with cliques of power users. It also actively discourages actually interesting discussions.

Look at the Stack Exchange network for an example of this. Or Wikipedia. (Or even Hacker News, to an extent.)

You restrict new and unpopular users, you end up driving away people who you probably shouldn't be driving away, and at the same time pulling in people who take it as a challenge. It also makes it harder to throw away accounts, which, again, discourages the interesting conversations while encouraging mindless content. Neither of those things are good.

You want karma, what do you do? You ~~~post~~~ spam low-effort posts/replies everywhere. You most certainly do not actually reply with though-provoking content, or, for that matter, longer replies. Because it isn't worth it. The more interesting the comment, the more likely you are to have people disagree with you and/or write a response instead of simply upvoting you and moving on. Instead you just see if you can be the first person with something vaguely half-decent and hope you get a comment where the votes start snowballing. I'm sure you've all seen it - the random 4 word reply that has 4x the karma of your next highest-voted post.

I do not believe that this is something that should be encouraged, and I believe that the current voting restrictions encourage this. This is not a problem now, but it will be. I believe that if the voting restrictions remain they will ultimately be the downfall of the site.
The restrictions for less popular users should be nixed
